# Open questions — exprim

What is not yet known, and what has since been answered.

## Open

### What in the published tree could still identify a private document?

`open` · `@exprim.privacy.residual-document-mentions/1`

Paths, file names and library directories are citations; working notes,
benchmark results and review page images are no longer tracked; document
nicknames in the changelogs were replaced by descriptions. What remains,
to accept or remove:

1. Fingerprints: `corpus/perf/manifest.json` and `pages.tsv` publish
   byte sizes, SHA-256 and per-page hashes of private documents. Anyone
   holding the same file can recognise it.
2. The bundled codecs carry their own benchmark records
   (`codecs/jbig2enc-rust/docs/benchmarks`, corpus specs) with short
   corpus nicknames and citations in place of paths, and one test and
   one example default to a nicknamed local directory.
3. Codec audit files record the home-directory checkout path of the
   machine that produced them (a user name and project directory, no
   document).
